title: Enforce current session authority on protected core authentication operations
owner_role: Authentication/backend owner + independent security reviewer + database/browser QA
current_state: P04-V02 independently confirmed nine current-authority failures: three private core-auth reads and one authentication-account deletion after both actual session revocation and database expiry, plus cached core-session disclosure after account deactivation. Each denied mutation deleted one synthetic authentication account; repair remains unimplemented and unauthorized. Query-override controls denied correctly. Browser/provider/supplementary evidence and wider production gates remain separate.
tasks: Refresh current auth catch-all, Better Auth configuration, core endpoint middleware and application guard call chains/hashes; reconcile exact endpoint behavior with P04-V02 evidence before editing.

Apply the smallest reviewed repair that requires current server-owned session and account eligibility for protected core reads/account mutations, preserving explicit anonymous authentication/recovery routes and legitimate signed-session operations.

Preserve the already working explicit disableCookieCache=true get-session, custom profile, tenant/module/media and query-tamper denials; do not infer a query-override exploit from source alone or edit installed dependency files as an untracked fix.

Requalify real signed-cache replay after session revocation, database expiry and relevant account-status changes; include authorized independent reads/writes and native before/after account/session/audit evidence.
Run selected actual browser recovery and provider continuity checks on a refreshed isolated build; obtain independent review and update P04-V02 evidence before advancing.
acceptance_criteria: Revoked/expired or ineligible current authority receives no private actor/account/session fields or sibling token metadata from admitted protected core endpoints.
Denied account mutations preserve all authentication accounts and unauthorized session/business state; intended security bookkeeping is separately classified.
Authorized independent core reads and account/profile operations remain functional; existing caller-query negative controls remain denied without weakening public sign-in/recovery.

Real session, browser, native database and source/build evidence remain distinct and bind the refreshed candidate; required P04-V02 requalification and other parent gates stay open until independently accepted.
rollback_recovery: Revert only owned repair while retaining production admission block; never restore weaker authority as an accepted release. Revoke synthetic sessions, stop owned local runtime/DB, retain evidence. No commit/push, production flags/data changes or deployment.
execution_boundary: One current-authority contract for protected core authentication operations. No implementation authorized by P04-V02 qualification. Broader browser freshness, provider, dependency upgrade or unrelated business changes require separate bounded review.
branch_pr_workflow: Future codex/ branch or explicitly owned local diff from approved candidate; inspect/stage only owned hunks if commit requested. PR/CI admin waits for authenticated authorization; never auto-merge/deploy.
